name: Power-Assisted Pedal Cycle, up to 200 W
description: The 200 W branch of Australia's national e-bike definition, which the states' road rules make a bicycle: a pedal cycle propelled mainly by human power, with electric motors of no more than 200 W combined maximum output that can't propel it on their own, weighing under 50 kg with a height-adjustable seat. It sets no speed limit. Since December 2025 it's no longer excluded from the road vehicles regulated on import unless it also meets EN 15194, and New South Wales and Queensland are dropping it from their road rules.

restrictions.rule: Designed to be propelled through a mechanism primarily using human power
restrictions.citation: Vehicle Standard (Australian Design Rule – Definitions and Vehicle Categories) 2005, cl. 3 (definition of power-assisted pedal cycle)

restrictions.rule: One or more auxiliary electric motors with a combined maximum power output of no more than 200 W; a combustion engine takes it out of the class
restrictions.citation: Vehicle Standard (Australian Design Rule – Definitions and Vehicle Categories) 2005, cl. 3 (definition of power-assisted pedal cycle)

restrictions.rule: Can't be propelled by the motors alone: the rider must pedal to set it or keep it in motion
restrictions.citation: Vehicle Standard (Australian Design Rule – Definitions and Vehicle Categories) 2005, cl. 3 (definition of power-assisted pedal cycle)

restrictions.rule: A tare mass, batteries included, of less than 50 kg, and a height-adjustable seat
restrictions.citation: Vehicle Standard (Australian Design Rule – Definitions and Vehicle Categories) 2005, cl. 3 (definition of power-assisted pedal cycle)

restrictions.rule: Excluded from the two- and three-wheeled moped categories (LA and LB)
restrictions.citation: Vehicle Standard (Australian Design Rule – Definitions and Vehicle Categories) 2005, cls. 4.2.1, 4.2.2

restrictions.rule: Past these limits a two-wheeler is a motor vehicle: an electric one that can't exceed 50 km/h is an LA moped, a faster one an LC motorcycle, and it can be ridden on a road or path only once it meets the Australian Design Rules and is registered, with a licensed rider
restrictions.citation: Vehicle Standard (Australian Design Rule – Definitions and Vehicle Categories) 2005, cls. 4.2.1, 4.2.3

restrictions.rule: The Australian Road Rules, the model the states' road rules follow, make it a bicycle, and exclude from bicycles any other vehicle with an auxiliary motor that can put out more than 200 W
restrictions.citation: Australian Road Rules, Dictionary (definition of bicycle); Road Safety Road Rules 2017 (Vic), Dictionary (definition of bicycle)

restrictions.rule: Ridden under the bicycle road rules, with no licence, registration or compulsory third-party insurance
No longer among the vehicles excluded from regulation as road vehicles unless it also meets EN 15194:2017 or a later edition, so importing one that doesn't may need a road vehicle approval
restrictions.citation: Road Vehicle Standards (Classes of Vehicles that are not Road Vehicles) Determination 2021, ss. 5(1), 6(h), as amended by F2025L01649; Road Vehicle Standards Act 2018, s. 6

restrictions.rule: Not a bicycle in New South Wales from 1 March 2029, when only an e-bike complying with EN 15194 is

Not a bicycle in Queensland, which since 1 July 2026 requires EN 15194 and a compliance label; one made before then that met Queensland's former power-assisted bicycle definition may be ridden until 28 February 2027
restrictions.citation: Transport Operations (Road Use Management) Act 1995 (Qld), s. 245, sch. 4; Transport Operations (Road Use Management—Accreditation and Other Provisions) Regulation 2015 (Qld), s. 177

restrictions.rule: Western Australia defines its own 200 W power assisted pedal cycle: designed to be propelled solely by human power, with auxiliary motors of no more than 200 W combined, and none of the national mass, seat or pedalling conditions
restrictions.citation: Road Traffic (Administration) Act 2008 (WA), s. 4; Road Traffic (Administration) Regulations 2014 (WA), r. 4(2)(b)

restrictions.rule: In Western Australia, a rider under 16 must not ride one with the power assistance engaged
Tasmania also lets a bicycle with a petrol motor of no more than 200 W be ridden, if it's propelled mainly by pedalling
